incidente.resumo: On July 12th, 2018, an attacker compromised the npm account of an ESLint maintainer and published malicious versions of eslint-scope and eslint-config-eslint whose postinstall script sent users' .npmrc contents, typically containing npm access tokens, to the attacker. The malicious versions were unpublished, the pastebin.com payload was taken down, a clean eslint-scope@3.7.3 was published, and npm revoked all access tokens issued before 2018-07-12 12:30 UTC.

descricao.texto: At 11:17 UTC on 2018-07-12 a user posted issue eslint/eslint-scope#39, notifying the ESLint team of the issue.
trechos: **2018-07-12 11:17 UTC**: A user posted eslint/eslint-scope#39, notifying the ESLint team of the issue.

descricao.texto: An attacker compromised the npm account of an ESLint maintainer, presumably using an email and password reused from a third-party breach; the account's password had been reused on several other sites and two-factor authentication was not enabled. The attacker generated an authentication token and used it to publish malicious versions eslint-config-eslint@5.0.2 and eslint-scope@3.7.2, whose postinstall script downloaded and executed code from pastebin.com that sent the user's .npmrc file to the attacker.
trechos: On July 12th, 2018, an attacker compromised the npm account of an ESLint maintainer and published malicious versions of the `eslint-scope` and `eslint-config-eslint` packages to the npm registry.
**Before the incident**: The attacker presumably found the maintainer’s reused email and password in a third-party breach and used them to log in to the maintainer’s npm account.
The maintainer whose account was compromised had reused their npm password on several other sites and did not have two-factor authentication enabled on their npm account.
**Early morning July 12th, 2018**: The attacker generated an authentication token in the maintainer’s npm account.

**2018-07-12 9:49 UTC**: The attacker used the generated authentication token to publish `eslint-config-eslint@5.0.2`, which contained a malicious `postinstall` script that attempts to exfiltrate the local machine’s `.npmrc` authentication token.
**2018-07-12 10:40 UTC**: The attacker published `eslint-scope@3.7.2`, which contained the same malicious `postinstall` script.
On installation, the malicious packages downloaded and executed code from `pastebin.com` which sent the contents of the user’s `.npmrc` file to the attacker.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: eslint-scope@3.7 is a dependency of several popular packages, including some older versions of eslint and the latest versions of babel-eslint and webpack.
trechos: - `eslint-scope@3.7`, a scope analysis library, is a dependency of several popular packages, including some older versions of `eslint` and the latest versions of `babel-eslint` and `webpack`.

passos.texto: At 12:27 UTC the pastebin.com link containing the malicious code was taken down.
trechos: **2018-07-12 12:27 UTC**: The pastebin.com link containing malicious code was taken down.

passos.texto: At 12:37 UTC the npm team unpublished eslint-scope@3.7.2 after being contacted by an ESLint maintainer; eslint-config-eslint@5.0.2 had been unpublished by the attacker at 10:25 UTC.
trechos: **2018-07-12 12:37 UTC**: The npm team unpublished `eslint-scope@3.7.2` after being contacted by an ESLint maintainer.
**2018-07-12 10:25 UTC**: The attacker unpublished `eslint-config-eslint@5.0.2`.

passos.texto: At 17:41 UTC the ESLint team published eslint-scope@3.7.3 with the code from eslint-scope@3.7.1 so that caches could pick up the new version.
trechos: **2018-07-12 17:41 UTC**: The ESLint team published `eslint-scope@3.7.3` with the code from `eslint-scope@3.7.1` so that caches could pick up the new version.

passos.texto: At 18:42 UTC npm revoked all access tokens generated before 2018-07-12 12:30 UTC, so tokens compromised by the attack should no longer be usable.
trechos: **2018-07-12 18:42 UTC**: npm revoked all access tokens generated before 2018-07-12 12:30 UTC.
As a result, all access tokens compromised by this attack should no longer be usable.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to package maintainers and users: avoid reusing the same password across multiple sites; a password manager can help.
trechos: - Package maintainers and users should avoid reusing the same password across multiple different sites.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to package maintainers: enable npm two-factor authentication.
trechos: - Package maintainers should enable npm two-factor authentication.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to package maintainers: audit and limit the number of people who have access to publish on npm.
trechos: - Package maintainers should audit and limit the number of people who have access to publish on npm.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to package maintainers: be careful with services that auto-merge dependency upgrades.
trechos: - Package maintainers should be careful with using any services that auto-merge dependency upgrades.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to application developers: use a lockfile (package-lock.json or yarn.lock) to prevent the auto-install of new packages.
trechos: - Application developers should use a lockfile (`package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock`) to prevent the auto-install of new packages.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to operators of their own npm registry: unpublish the malicious versions of each package.
trechos: If you run your own npm registry, you should unpublish the malicious versions of each package.

motivo_confianca_baixa: categoria_causa: 'credential-auth' (compromised npm account credentials) vs 'supply-chain' (tampered packages published from the npm registry ran in users' environments).
observacoes: All prevention items are recommendations to others (maintainers, users, developers, registry operators); the document lists no commitments by the ESLint team itself. The 'Attack Method' section only links to details elsewhere.
